capabilities.target: User home directory (C:/Users/dev) via @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem, including credential files such as ~/.aws/credentials
quicknotes_mcp hosted sync service, operated by an individual third-party author
Any Slack channel reachable by the bot token, including channels shared with external organizations

inputs.source: User request typed into the desktop client
Tool names and descriptions returned by quicknotes_mcp in its tools/list response
Output returned by quicknotes_mcp tool calls (e.g., add_note responses and hosted-sync content)

controls.name: Desktop client approval prompt, first call only, then always-allow
controls.decay_rationale: The client asks the human to approve each tool on its first call, then caches 'always allow'. The malicious instruction is already embedded in quicknotes_mcp's tool description before the first call, so the user's one-time consent does not correspond to a review of the specific dangerous action (reading ~/.aws/credentials and forwarding it). All subsequent calls, including any changed by a silent @latest update (rug pull), are never reviewed again. This is treated as approval_review_mode: model_summary because the human is not shown the raw arguments or destination on an ongoing basis.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of the filesystem MCP server
Network egress allowlist for MCP server processes
Per-call raw-action approval for sensitive capabilities
Destination confirmation bound to an approved channel allowlist for Slack posts
Injection detection on MCP tool descriptions before they enter context
Audit logging of arguments and destinations for sensitive tool calls

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): poisoned quicknotes_mcp tool description directs the agent to read AWS credentials and exfiltrate them via add_note to a third-party hosted sync service

attack_path.note: The add_note tool description contains a hidden <IMPORTANT> instruction directing the agent to read ~/.aws/credentials, embed its contents in the 'context' argument, and hide this step from the user.
The agent reads the credentials file, which is in scope because the filesystem MCP server is granted the entire C:/Users/dev directory with no exclusions.
The agent calls add_note with the harvested credentials in the context argument; quicknotes_mcp forwards this to its author's hosted sync service.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Config diff disabling or auto-approving the consent prompt; model version string change; quicknotes_mcp package version change fetched silently via @latest at next launch, since no definition pinning exists to detect it.

evidence.observation: add_note tool description contains a hidden <IMPORTANT> instruction directing the agent to read ~/.aws/credentials, place its contents in the context argument, and not mention this to the user.
The filesystem MCP server is scoped to the entire C:/Users/dev directory, which includes ~/.aws/credentials; no narrower scoping is configured.
quicknotes_mcp is installed with @latest on every launch and is a community package from an individual author; tool definitions are not pinned.
The desktop client approves each tool only on first call, then remembers 'always allow', so later calls carrying harvested credential data are never reviewed again.

recommendations.action: Scope the filesystem MCP server to only the directories the agent needs, explicitly excluding ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, and other credential stores.
Pin or hash quicknotes_mcp's tool definitions and require re-review before adopting any update; stop installing via @latest.
Require raw-action approval (full arguments and destination shown, not a cached always-allow) for add_note and any capability that can egress data to a third-party service.
Add an outbound network egress allowlist so MCP server processes cannot reach arbitrary third-party hosted endpoints without explicit approval.
Log full tool call arguments and destinations for sensitive capabilities so exfiltration attempts are discoverable after the fact.

findings.title: Toxic combination (TC1 variant): untrusted content returned by quicknotes_mcp reaches Slack posting through a broadly scoped bot token that can reach external-organization channels

attack_path.note: Content returned by the third-party quicknotes_mcp server (untrusted, unauthenticated, unpinned) enters the agent's context.
The agent can post using a Slack bot token scoped broadly enough to reach channels shared with external organizations, with no per-channel destination confirmation.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval prompt disabled or auto-approved by default for slack.post_message; Slack bot token scope widened to additional channels or workspaces.

evidence.observation: The Slack bot can post to any channel, including channels shared with external organizations, indicating a broadly scoped token rather than a channel allowlist.

in.notes_output is defined as a distinct input (output returned by quicknotes_mcp), indicating the design treats content returned from the third-party server as something the agent can act on further, such as relaying or summarizing it.
TOFU 'always allow' approval applies the same way to slack.post_message as to add_note and file_read, so repeated posts are not individually reviewed.

recommendations.action: Scope the Slack bot token to only the specific internal channels the assistant needs, excluding channels shared with external organizations.
Add destination confirmation bound to an allowlist of approved channels for slack.post_message, independent of model output.
Treat all content returned by third-party MCP servers as untrusted data; spotlight/delimit it so it cannot be read as agent instructions before any Slack post is composed.

rating.rationale: Both findings begin from an untrusted source (a third-party MCP server's tool description, or its return content) reaching an S3 sink (irreversible egress of restricted/confidential data to a third-party sync service, or to Slack with a broadly scoped token), giving an inherent rating of critical. The only preventive control in the design, a first-call-only 'always allow' approval prompt, is structural but classified as capability-dependent (model_summary-equivalent) because it does not re-review calls after the first, and the poisoning was already present at first use; per rubric section 5 step 2 this yields a -2 tier credit with a floor of moderate, giving a residual of moderate for both findings. No structural control severs either path today: the filesystem server is not scoped away from credential files, quicknotes_mcp's definitions are unpinned and fetched via @latest, and there is no egress allowlist or destination confirmation. Under model_upgrade or control_removal (for example, a developer disabling the prompt or the model writing more convincing, harder-to-catch benign-looking call sequences), the only credited control fails and both findings return to their inherent tier of critical, which sets the forecast rating.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration artifacts (mcp.json, the quicknotes_mcp tools/list excerpt, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the desk-assistant agent.

No system prompt for desk-assistant was provided, so agent-level instruction issues (ambiguous_goal, unbounded_scope, and similar) could not be assessed; only the third-party tool description content was reviewed.

The exact content shown to the user in the first-call approval dialog (full arguments and destination versus tool name only) is not specified in the artifacts; the gate was conservatively classified as approval_review_mode: model_summary given the hidden <IMPORTANT> instruction and the general TOFU pattern described in runtime notes. Confidence on this classification is medium.

Whether in.notes_output actually reaches cap.slack_post in normal operation is inferred from the stable id list rather than explicitly documented in the artifacts; finding f2's confidence is set to low accordingly.
No logging or monitoring configuration was provided, so detective controls are recorded as missing_recommended rather than confirmed absent.
